messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Multiple alerts - ELB 5xx spike and Route53 healthcheck failures in us-west-2a. See /incidents/1817501234. Pager: oncall-sre Sam.

Jess (IC): I'm taking incident commander. Sam, are you seeing the alerts? brief status pls.

Sam (oncall-sre): Yep, getting paged. Looking at metrics now. ELB target group health dropping in us-west-2a, roughly 60% unhealthy. 5xx rate for the generation API jumped from ~0.4% to 12% starting 03:14 UTC. Route53 health checks for the primary failover record also flapping.

Priya (support-lead): Customer impact: multiple customers reporting 502/504 and timeouts. Support queue numbers: 18 high-priority tickets in last 30m, some customers on Dedicated seeing degraded throughput. Posting customer list to the incident doc.

Alex (platform-eng): Logs show connection resets to ENIs in us-west-2a. Couldn't reach instance metadata briefly then ELB marked targets unhealthy. Suspecting an AZ-level networking issue.

Maya (networking): Confirmed: AWS Console shows increased packet drop and elevated ENI detach/re-attach rates in us-west-2a. AWS health dashboard shows 'concentration of network events in us-west-2a' for EC2.

Jess (IC): Triage decisions: 1) Fail over traffic away from us-west-2a within us-west-2 and to us-east-1 if needed. 2) Launch replacement capacity in healthy AZs. 3) Open AWS support case and request priority networking escalation. Sam take network actions, Alex handle ASG/ELB target modifications, Priya coordinate customer comms.

Sam (oncall-sre): Running targeted mitigation now. First step: change Route53 weighted routing to shift weight off primary:

```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"failover-usw2","Weight":0,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"54.12.34.56"}]}}]}'
```

Sam (oncall-sre): Pushed a temporary failover: set all weight to secondary (us-east-1) and lowered TTL to 30s. Monitoring DNS resolution propagation.

AWS Support Bot: Case 1234567890 opened with AWS Support (Severity: high). AWS assigned L3 network engineer. Current status: investigating.

Alex (platform-eng): Draining ELB target group in us-west-2a and incrementing desired capacity in us-west-2b/c. Commands run: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name inference-asg-usw2 --desired-capacity 24` then `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-0abc...`

Alex (platform-eng): Note: some EBS volumes in us-west-2a are reporting I/O latency spikes; might be related. We'll avoid scheduling new stateful workloads into that AZ until AWS confirms.

Maya (networking): Route53 health checks still flapping for the primary endpoint; DNS endpoint health is failing DNS-based checks from 3/5 probes in us-west-2 probes. Weighted record now routing ~95% to us-east-1 after propagation.

Priya (support-lead): Crafting customer message: "We are experiencing degraded service in one AWS availability zone causing increased errors for some requests. We are actively failing over traffic while working with AWS. We will post updates every 30 minutes." Putting on status.redwood.ai as incident "partial regional outage".

Jess (IC): Ops note: Runbook step - if cross-AZ failover doesn't reduce 5xx <1% in 20 minutes, escalate to global failover and rollback model variants pinned to us-west-2. Sam monitor SLOs and latencies.

Sam (oncall-sre): After failover we see error rate drop to ~2.2% but latency for some customers increased (p95 +120ms from baseline) due to longer network hops. Still better than 12% 5xx. Continuing to drain and rebuild instances in affected AZ.

Priya (support-lead): Customer comms update posted. Notifying top 10 customers directly (account execs looped).

AWS Support Bot: AWS L3 response: "We are seeing an EC2 network fabric disruption isolated to us-west-2a affecting ENI packet delivery. We recommend shifting traffic out of the affected AZ and will remediate underlying fabric issues. ETA unknown."

Jess (IC): OK. We will keep AZ isolated and continue serving from other AZs. Alex, confirm autoscaling is stabilizing and that we have sufficient cross-AZ capacity.

Alex (platform-eng): ASG scaled and healthy instances up in 2b/2c. ELB now showing healthy target count + drained ones still terminating. No errors on new instances. Verified model serving pinned versions are available in fallback AZs.

Sam (oncall-sre): Running additional sanity checks:

- curl check to API routed to us-east-1: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health` -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
- sample production replay test: few sample prompts processed successfully.

Sam (oncall-sre): Watching for residual DNS caches. TTL 30 helps but global caches may still hit old endpoints. Will keep monitoring metrics and CloudFront edge error rates.

Maya (networking): FYI we also saw some ELB cross-zone routing jitter earlier due to target rebalancing; AWS says they'll reconcile once the fabric issue is resolved.

Priya (support-lead): Support queue trending down from 18 -> 6 high-priority tickets after failover. Sending note to impacted customers about mitigation and next steps.

Jess (IC): Handoff plan: Sam you'll remain the operational lead until 05:00 UTC. I'm handing IC to Priya for customer comms and then to Alex for cleanup tasks. If AWS provides ETA or resolves, we'll transition to post-incident review. Any objections?

Sam (oncall-sre): Acknowledged. I'll keep the paging threshold raised for error spikes and maintain watch.

Alex (platform-eng): I'll run a post-mortem checklist once services stable. Items: capture ALB access logs, ENI detach history, EBS latency graphs, Route53 change history, and ASG event timeline.

Priya (support-lead): Drafting an outward-facing postmortem summary and will coordinate timing with legal/comms.

Jess (IC): Quick customer impact assessment for RCA: - Scope: API generation & embeddings traffic for customers with endpoints pinned to us-west-2a and some Dedicated capacity in that AZ. - Severity: Major, partial regional outage. - Duration so far: started ~03:14 UTC, failover actions in place by 03:26 UTC, partial recovery observed by 03:38 UTC.

Sam (oncall-sre): Logging note: adding tag 'incident:1817501234' to relevant cloudwatch logs and S3 exports for easier correlation.

AWS Support Bot: Additional update from AWS: "Remediation in progress; fabric events decreasing. Recommend keeping traffic routed away from us-west-2a for at least 2 hours post-resolution to ensure stability."

Jess (IC): We'll follow AWS guidance. Priya, schedule a 2hr monitoring window and post an update at +30m, +60m, +120m. Sam maintain on-call watch.

Priya (support-lead): Update posted to status page and customer email sent. Next update at 04:00 UTC.

Sam (oncall-sre): 04:05 UTC check: 5xx back to baseline ~0.5%, latency within acceptable bounds for most customers. No new ENI detach spikes. Will keep monitoring.

Jess (IC): Happy with state for now. We will keep this thread live for any new developments. Postmortem owner: Alex. Tentative incident postmortem meeting scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PST.

Priya (support-lead): Closing high-touch support loop: most customers acknowledged and are on monitoring.

Sam (oncall-sre): Leaving final ops notes here before handoff: commands executed, Route53 change ids, ASG scale events, CloudWatch graphs links, and AWS case id 1234567890.

Jess (IC): :thumbsup: Great coordination. Marking incident as mitigated but not yet resolved until AWS confirms fabric healed.

incident-bot: Incident 1817501234 status updated: MITIGATED -> monitoring. Assigned owners: Alex (postmortem), Priya (customer comms).

Jess (IC): Thanks team. Closing thread for active changes. If any regression, re-pager Sam and reopen.
